article_title: Publication in a medical student journal predicts short- and long-term academic success: a matched-cohort study.
citation: Al-Busaidi Ibrahim S., Wells Cameron I., Wilkinson Tim J. (2019). Publication in a medical student journal predicts short- and long-term academic success: a matched-cohort study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1704-x
title: New Zealand Medical Student Journal (NZMSJ) as a venue for student-authored research and early peer-review experience
description: The NZMSJ is a student-run medical journal publishing original contributions (research papers, review articles, case reports) and non-original contributions (feature/perspective articles, book/media reviews, conference reports) written by New Zealand medical students. It "employs a double-blind peer-review process undertaken by a combination of student and expert reviewers" and is indexed in Google Scholar, having published over 300 articles since its 2003 launch. This study evaluated its association with graduates' later academic outcomes.
requirements: Student authors identified via author biographies; double-blind peer review by student and expert reviewers
constraints: Predominantly caters for medical students from New Zealand, which the authors state limits generalizability of findings to other cohorts and MSJs
examples: The study hand-searched NZMSJ archives (Issues 1–14, 2004–2011), identifying 50 student-authored publications (26 literature reviews, 22 original research articles, and 2 case reports) by 49 unique student authors
